stem: Aryan lists the factors of three whole numbers: $1$ has only $\{1\}$; $11$ has $\{1,11\}$; $15$ has $\{1,3,5,15\}$.

options.text: Call $1$ a composite number from the label composite alone.
$1$ is neither (one factor); $11$ is prime (exactly two factors); $15$ is composite (more than two factors).
Say the prime and composite labels are what produce these factor lists.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: Classification follows the number of factors: one factor means neither, exactly two means prime, and more than two means composite.

teacher.key_rationale: Factor count decides the class. Relabelling 1 as composite, or saying the labels create the lists, miss that hinge.
